title: Grateful Dead Live at New Haven Coliseum on 1979-10-25
lineage: Set 1: Dat (Sony D8) -> CD (Tascam CDRW700) -> EAC -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHN Set 2: Master Dat (Sony R500) -> Behringer UltraMatch SRC 2000 -> SEK'D Prodif Plus -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional ->  SHN (3 Discs Audio / 2 Discs SHN)
source: Set 1: Nakamichi 700 -> Cassette Master -> Dat (Recorded By Steve Rolfe) Set 2: SBD -> Master Cassette (Sony TCD5M/Maxell UDXL II) -> Master Dat (Panasonic SV3800/48k)

ai_review.summary: Hybrid audience/board tape delivers crystal‑clear second set with a monster Shakedown Street and standout Passenger, while the first‑set crowd mic is boomy.
ai_review.review: The show shines in its second half where the soundboard feed captures a ripping Shakedown Street, an inspired Passenger, and a tight Estimated, highlighted by a trippy pre‑drums space after a solid Eyes. The first set’s audience recording adds atmosphere but suffers from boominess, and a few listeners note a chaotic space segment that borders on a meltdown. Overall the performance is strong for the era, though the abrupt ending into Good Lovin’ leaves some wanting more.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical highlights and the clear board recording of set 2, while only a few note issues with the audience tape or an over‑experimental space segment.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Set 1 is an audience tape – boomy hall ambience and occasional crowd yells add immediacy but reduce clarity. Set 2 is a soundboard feed – crystal‑clear mix with excellent instrument separation. Some listeners describe the space segment as chaotic, suggesting possible mixing or performance anomalies.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows superbly with pre‑drums space after Eyes leading into a monster Shakedown Street; the abrupt transition out of the show into Good Lovin’ is the only notable dip.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia praised for shredding on Shakedown Street and Passenger, plus a memorable ending guitar break.
band_member_comments.Keys: One reviewer blames Brent (keys) for a “meltdown” sounding like a horror‑film soundtrack during the space segment.
